oil.summary: Crude posted its fourth consecutive session of gains, with WTI settling at $80.24/bbl (+1.13%) and Brent at $85.72/bbl (+1.17%), extending a near 9-10% weekly rally driven by escalating US-Iran hostilities. Three tankers were damaged in the Gulf, Hormuz shipping risk was raised to severe, and the collapsed US-Iran ceasefire prompted Trump to threaten strikes on Iranian energy targets while expanding sanctions targeting the Shamkhani network. A 1.7-million-barrel draw in US crude inventories (week ending July 10) added fuel, and Brent futures flipped into backwardation for the first time in a month, signalling tight prompt supply. On the Russian side, ~135 million barrels remain stranded at sea following Ukraine's airstrike campaign on refineries, while a bipartisan Senate bill targets Russia's shadow fleet. RBOB and heating oil both shed roughly 3.7% on the day despite the crude bid, a divergence worth monitoring. The monthly reading for WTI remains down 5.47%, underscoring how sharp this week's geopolitical premium has been.
drivers: US-Iran conflict intensifying: tanker strikes in the Gulf, Hormuz shipping risk raised to severe, and renewed US sanctions on Iran's oil network
~135 million barrels of Russian crude stranded at sea amid Ukraine's tanker/refinery strike campaign, compounding supply-side tightness
US crude inventories fell 1.7 million barrels for the week ending July 10; Brent curve flipped into backwardation signalling tight prompt supply

gas.summary: Natural gas price action today presented a stark divergence between US and European benchmarks. Henry Hub edged up a modest 0.65% to $2.923/MMBtu, though the contract remains deeply in the red over the past week (-9.00%) and month (-6.31%), suggesting domestic fundamentals remain bearish. TTF, by contrast, surged 3.28% to €52.959/MWh and is up 13.70% on the week, likely reflecting European anxiety over Middle East supply route disruptions stemming from the Hormuz crisis and broader geopolitical stress. News flow directly relevant to the gas sector today is thin; the sole headline concerns a floating wind technology debut in China aimed at powering oil rigs. Traders should treat the Henry Hub/TTF spread widening as the primary story here.
drivers: TTF rallied sharply (+3.28% on the day, +13.70% on the week), likely reflecting European supply-risk premium tied to the Hormuz crisis
Henry Hub remains under pressure on a weekly (-9.00%) and monthly (-6.31%) basis, indicating bearish US domestic fundamentals
Direct gas-specific news flow today is minimal; the TTF move appears to be importing risk premia from the oil/geopolitical complex

power.summary: The power and carbon complex offered a mixed but eventful session. EU EUAs dipped marginally (-0.28%) to $76.815, though the contract holds modest weekly and monthly gains. The dominant structural story is PJM's capacity auction falling 6.8 GW short for a third consecutive year as data-centre load growth continues to overwhelm grid planning. China connected what is described as the world's largest hybrid solar plant to the grid, a signal of accelerating capacity build-out. Engie Brasil raised $1.66 billion in a share offering, underscoring continued private capital appetite for power infrastructure. On the nuclear front, a data breach exposed ~19,000 sensitive files from India's Kudankulam plant, and Kazakhstan's atomic energy chief is touring Chinese nuclear facilities amid expanding Sino-Central Asian energy partnerships. The Iran/Hormuz collapse is also reshaping power-sector planning, with a separate piece noting China actively hedging its energy exposure.
drivers: PJM capacity auction came up 6.8 GW short for a third straight year as data-centre demand growth outpaces supply commitments, raising medium-term reliability concerns

China grid-connected the world's largest hybrid solar plant and is expanding nuclear partnerships in Central Asia, reinforcing the shift in energy-security strategy away from Middle East oil dependency
Iran port blockade and Hormuz crisis are pressuring European gas (TTF +13.70% on the week), which feeds through to carbon via fuel-switching economics, even as EUAs held nearly flat today
